supported_pattern: Both policies fail during reach before any grasp or instruction switch; all ten native cumulative-force terminations; all minimum distances exceed the frozen 0.08 m grasp-switch threshold. Candidate minimum distance improves in 2/5 seeds and worsens in 3/5. No native success improvement observed.
limitations: Five fixed development seeds, no significance test or population inference.
Different episode lengths: terminal force and raw clip totals are not exposure-controlled comparative metrics.
Base-frame displacement is not world-frame object motion; collision location and cause are not established.
Candidate seed2027 ends at19 actions; its step20 window is unavailable, not imputed.
Offline dev8 improvement did not produce native task success; this does not identify architecture or training-data root cause.

next_week_single_experiment.name: Fixed candidate paired base-motion clamp intervention
next_week_single_experiment.question: Does suppressing mobile-base commands reduce early contact-force accumulation enough to expose arm-only approach behavior, or does reach remain inadequate?
next_week_single_experiment.design: On the same five native initial states, compare unchanged frozen step250 against step250 with only mobile-base translation/yaw commands set to zero after normal clipping; keep arm/torso/gripper, observations, RNG, prompts and native termination unchanged. No learning, scaling search or checkpoint selection. Fresh processes, fixed 20-action cap per episode.
next_week_single_experiment.readout: Compare force accumulated at the largest common completed action index up to19, TCP-object distance change and identified contact links; separately record early native termination. Save world-frame base/TCP/object poses to distinguish base-relative coordinate change from object displacement.
next_week_single_experiment.interpretation: A force reduction with impaired approach would show a mobility/contact tradeoff under intervention, not prove a root cause or improve the benchmark. Unchanged force would weaken a simple base-command explanation. This is a diagnostic ablation, never counted as original-protocol native success.
